stimulus:
Shards (do not explain them; let them collide with the problem):

- a tardigrade's glassy sugar-shell, trehalose, waiting out a decade
- the bell-founder tuning a bell by shaving its lip, not its crown
- lichen: two kingdoms signing a lease
- salt-cured ink; the slow bloom of iron-gall through paper
- a ferryman who counts only the empty seats
- kintsugi: the repair is the most valuable part
- dowsing rod / null result / dowsing rod
- slime mold re-drawing a subway map overnight
- negative space of a key
- the dead reckoning of a shepherd's dog
- moiré: two ordinary grids, one extravagant pattern
- a cheese rind as a country with borders
- antifragile-ish, semi-forgotten, pre-measured, un-averaged
- the audience that applauds in the wrong place
- a tide table written for a river that no longer exists
- ant cemetery geometry; whale-fall ecosystems; rust as a clock
- translate: "noise" to "tenant"; "error" to "guest"; "control" to "weather"

Instruction to self: pick the two shards least related to the question, treat each as a literal working mechanism, and ask what the research problem would look like if it operated that way. Prefer ideas that would make a specialist say "wait, why hasn't anyone tried that?"

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Bell-lip tuning: perturb enhancer edges, not the AP-1 core
ideas.description: Instead of knocking out AP-1 (the crown), use CRISPR base editing or dCas9 to subtly alter AP-1 motif flanks, spacing, and affinity at the lip of primed enhancers, then quantify how the strength and duration of a stimulus-induced memory response (accessibility via ATAC, transcriptional re-induction kinetics) shift. A graded, tunable dose-response of memory to motif affinity would show AP-1 sequence encodes memory rather than just being required for activation.

ideas.title: Negative-space footprinting of AP-1 after it leaves
ideas.description: After transient stimulation (e.g., TPA, wounding signal, or inflammatory cue) and AP-1 washout, use CUT&Tag/CUT&RUN for AP-1 factors alongside ATAC footprinting, histone marks (H3K4me1, H3K27ac) and the SWI/SNF (BAF) complex to map the 'key-shaped hole': accessible, BAF-marked sites that retain open chromatin once AP-1 is gone. Compare days to weeks later and with acute AP-1 degradation (dTAG/auxin degron) to test whether the memory persists independent of continued AP-1 binding or needs it to be maintained.

ideas.title: Trehalose-style dormancy: AP-1 memory across quiescence and division
ideas.description: Prime cells, then push them into quiescence (serum starvation or contact inhibition) or through multiple cell cycles, holding for days to weeks with no AP-1 activity (monitored by live AP-1 reporters). Re-challenge and test whether primed loci retain the faster, stronger response and whether mitotic bookmarking by AP-1 (live-cell imaging, mitotic-chromosome ChIP) explains persistence, with degron removal of AP-1 during dormancy as the causal control.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-traced memory with un-averaged readouts
ideas.description: Combine barcoded lineage tracing with single-cell multiome (scRNA + scATAC) to compare sister cells after a primary stimulus and re-stimulus, testing whether the response of a sister predicts the other's response beyond what shared AP-1 dynamics predict. Heritable, clone-specific, bimodal memory states that track with AP-1-dependent accessibility would be invisible in bulk averages and would distinguish true cellular memory from persistent signaling.

ideas.title: Slime-mold rewiring: optogenetic AP-1 pulse-pattern training
ideas.description: Use optogenetic control of AP-1 (e.g., light-inducible c-Fos/c-Jun or upstream kinases) to deliver defined pulse trains of varying frequency, duration and spacing, then measure whether later responses depend on the history of the pattern, like a network re-routing its paths after use. Pair with live reporters of target genes and ATAC to build a history-to-state map and test for hallmarks of memory: dependence on training pattern, spacing effects, decay time, and erasure by counter-stimuli.
